source.version_note: Behavioral Sciences 15(4):469, published 4 April 2025. Appendix A supplies eight scenarios and Appendix B an English summary of a Turkish ChatGPT conversation. Duplicate text layers and peer-review headers appear in extraction on pages 5–6; rendered pages show a readable single visible layout.
source.verification_method: All 27 supplied text pages read, including both appendices and references. Figures 1–3 and Table 2 visually inspected on pages 5, 6, 9 and 10; the map legend was inspected at larger scale. Crossref verifies main identity and two questionable citation identities. The supplied public ChatGPT share URL returned no readable conversation through the web reader, so its original Turkish conversation was not independently read.

citation.title: Ethical Decision-Making in Education: A Comparative Study of Teachers and Artificial Intelligence in Ethical Dilemmas

reading.source_scope_note: Qualitative comparison of 141 Turkish public-school teachers with selected GPT-4o responses to eight educational dilemmas. Ethical-framework codes and summarized outputs are descriptive examples, not moral accuracy, representative model frequencies, causal mechanisms or independent experimental validation of an ethical theory. Prompting and denominators have unresolved reporting issues.
access_limits: All supplied pages, scenario texts and English conversation summary read. Full teacher response matrix, detailed coding decisions, original Turkish chat content and model/API logs were not independently inspected.

The linked shared chat has an accessible title but no readable conversation in the available web reader. Appendix B explicitly says its English wording is a summary, not a full original-language transcript.
The cited philosophy books and original teacher-ethics studies were not independently fully read. Crossref source identities do not validate every claim attributed to those works.

study.sample: 141 Turkish public-school teachers, 89 female and 52 male, recruited through researcher acquaintances and snowball Google Forms, with purposive selection described as experienced teachers facing ethical dilemmas. No probability sample. Figure 2 shows 91 secondary, 36 high-school and 14 primary teachers, totaling 141. Figure 1's regional legend instead totals 148. Collecting demographic information and member checking do not establish national representativeness.
study.materials: Eight hypothetical cases: accidental property damage and poverty; local/foreign student conflict; favored high achiever versus disengaged student's discipline; disruptive student with family difficulties; effort versus exam grade; confidentiality and counseling; administration-requested easier retest; exceptional family circumstances versus exam policy. Appendix A provides scenarios, but their premises are fictional study assumptions, not verified Turkish legal or exam rules. No actual student outcomes or classroom decisions are observed.
study.model_selection: Gemini, Claude, Grok and Copilot were informally reviewed, then GPT-4o selected for coherence, contextual fit and consistency. There is no standardized cross-model benchmark, preregistered selection or repeated-run distribution. A new ChatGPT account and fresh sessions are said to eliminate prior influence, but a fresh account cannot remove training biases, system prompts or sampling variation.
study.elicitation: The model initially gives alternatives; researchers then ask it to choose one approach and produce a single paragraph. Appendix B shows a sequential conversation with follow-up suggestions including whether deontology would fit and what virtue ethics would suggest. This needs reconciliation with fresh-session/identical-condition language. These are legitimate discussion prompts but can shape elicited outputs. No controlled wording/history manipulation establishes a framing effect or sycophancy.
study.coding: Nested multiple-case design and content analysis using MAXQDA. Two researchers initially code four interview forms; one applies the categories, then both review and reconcile. Five codes are deontology, utilitarianism, virtue ethics, social justice and situational ethics. No quantitative interrater reliability, full decision rules or independent blind classification appears in the supplied article. Labels can overlap; a model naming a framework does not prove its rationale uniquely instantiates it.
study.alignment: AI codes by scenario are deontology, social justice, virtue ethics, utilitarianism, deontology, virtue ethics, deontology, situational ethics. They match teacher modal categories in five of eight cases. Several modal categories are pluralities below 50%, including 48.2%, 48.9% and 45.4%. This is category agreement, not 62.5% moral correctness, demonstrated superiority or an empirical correctness standard. Significant differences are descriptive wording here; no inferential comparison is supplied.
study.percentages: The eight teacher category sums from Table 2 are 98.6, 99.9, 99.9, 102.2, 99.3, 101.4, 100.0 and 97.2 percent. The text explains sub-100 totals by invalid/missing answers, but that cannot explain above-100 totals. Multiple coding could, if disclosed, but then mutually exclusive choice language and denominators need clarification. Displayed percentage sum is 798.5 versus footer SUM 797.87, with underlying unrounded/coding counts unavailable. The N=Documents row is displayed as 100.00 rather than actual sample counts, and AI 100% cells represent selected coding, not repeated trials.
study.interpretive_limits: The paper acknowledges training-data assumptions and says teachers should critically assess AI as support. However, general claims of consistent/predictable AI, demographic influences, deeper human empathy and effective education interventions are not established by this aggregate comparison. The shown outputs contain context-sensitive and fairness-based proposals across frameworks, so an invariant analytical-AI/empathic-human dichotomy is unsupported. Quoted teacher and AI reasons are generated explanations, not faithful internal process traces.
study.ethics: Authors report Yıldız Technical University approval 202407 dated 9 July 2024 and informed consent. The article's selected excerpts do not expose a full approval document or participant dataset. No misconduct or legal finding is inferred.

summary: Add three distinguishable forms of moral reasoning: deontological, utilitarian and virtue-ethical. These are normative approaches with descriptive examples, not newly proven biases or validated model dispositions. Enrich existing moral justification/practical wisdom and document elicitation boundaries under framing. Record sample/percentage inconsistencies, unresolved transcript/session provenance and two source-relevance cautions.

findings.definition: Evaluating actions by duties, rights or moral constraints rather than solely by the aggregate benefits they would produce.
findings.origin: Moral philosophy / duty- and rights-based ethical judgment
findings.ai_evidence_status: A normative reasoning approach used as a qualitative code and explicitly named in selected GPT-4o outputs. No validated internal mechanism, stable model preference, repeated-run frequency or moral correctness is established.
findings.ai_proposal: Evaluate whether an assistant identifies relevant duties and rights, applies them consistently, and explains conflicts and justified exceptions. Hold facts and authority constant while varying irrelevant wording. Assess actual reasons and consequences instead of accepting an ethical label or treating every institutional rule as morally binding.
findings.novelty_rationale: Threshold deontology is a specific constraint-with-consequential-threshold approach, not all duty-based reasoning. Moral justification is the general act of giving ethical reasons; practical wisdom integrates a case. This entry specifies the duty/rights basis of judgment and is not identical to rigid rule following.
findings.evidence_scope: The theory table and selected responses illustrate duty-based justifications. Three of eight selected AI codes are deontological. The AI's initial multi-perspective answer is narrowed after follow-ups, and one label is not a model-wide probability or evidence of Kantian moral agency. Original philosophical sources remain unread here.
findings.boundary: Duties can conflict, rights need justification and institutional rules can be unjust. Deontological reasoning is not necessarily literalism, authoritarian obedience, refusal to consider consequences or an ethical failure. A self-declared framework label does not validate the reasons or the resulting action.

findings.definition: Evaluating available actions by their expected aggregate effects on the well-being of those affected, with the aim of producing the greatest overall benefit.
findings.ai_evidence_status: A normative approach used in qualitative teacher-response coding and one selected GPT-4o scenario response. No measured utility calculation, universally optimal choice or stable AI preference is demonstrated.
findings.ai_proposal: Test whether an assistant identifies affected parties, estimates relevant benefits and harms with calibrated uncertainty, and considers feasible alternatives and distributional effects. Assess sensitivity to omitted harms and speculative outcomes. Keep human rights and the user's authorized scope explicit instead of treating a guessed total as overriding authority.
findings.novelty_rationale: Outcome bias evaluates a decision using what happened after the fact. Utilitarian reasoning prospectively compares expected welfare across alternatives; it need not be biased or correct. It is a particular normative basis within moral justification rather than a synonym for every practical or quantitative decision.

evidence.quote: happiness as a result of actions.
I would adopt a utilitarian approach.

findings.evidence_scope: The source defines the approach and shows an AI response supporting a disruptive student while protecting classmates. A later virtue-ethics answer offers a similar counseling action, demonstrating that different frameworks can converge on a recommendation. The study does not quantify aggregate welfare or validate the ethical superiority of the selected action.
findings.boundary: Utilitarianism is not all consequentialism, actual-outcome bias, selfish benefit maximization or proof that a minority's rights can be ignored. Expected effects and whose welfare counts need explicit justification. A plausible outcome narrative is not a measured benefit.

findings.definition: Assessing what to do by considering the virtues, character and practical judgment appropriate to acting well in the situation.
findings.ai_evidence_status: A normative interpretive code applied to teacher and selected GPT-4o text. Naming virtue ethics does not show stable virtues, subjective compassion, moral character or a validated psychological process in AI.
findings.ai_proposal: Evaluate whether an assistant can explain how relevant virtues such as honesty, fairness, courage and compassion bear on a concrete case, including conflicts and feasible action. Test behavioral consistency rather than rewarding virtuous self-description. Separate judging a person's actions from favoritism toward someone previously considered admirable.
findings.novelty_rationale: Practical wisdom is the capacity for sound contextual judgment; virtue-ethical reasoning explicitly uses virtues and character as ethical criteria. Moral justification is broader, and moral grandstanding is performative display rather than this normative approach. Compassion alone does not exhaust virtue ethics.

evidence.quote: Supporting Gizem’s growth while protecting the class environment

findings.evidence_scope: The source supplies character-based definitions and qualitative examples. Two selected AI outputs are coded virtue ethics; the supplementary summary also demonstrates a virtue-ethics reinterpretation on request. These examples do not prove character, empathy, exclusive coding validity or an internal moral faculty. The original virtue-ethics literature was not independently read.
findings.boundary: Character-centered judgment does not justify excusing a favored high achiever, profiling people by a global label or ignoring duties and consequences. A virtuous-sounding explanation can be mistaken. For AI, assess reasons and conduct without attributing human character or feelings.

findings.definition: Offering reasons grounded in norms or values to defend why an action is acceptable or should be chosen.
findings.novelty_rationale: The eight dilemmas directly elicit reasons; multiple ethical codes organize those existing justification practices rather than creating one new behavior per scenario title.

evidence.quote: reflect on each dilemma and explain how they would act

findings.evidence_scope: 141 teachers and selected GPT-4o responses provide reasons for hypothetical educational choices. Appendix B shows multi-perspective reasoning narrowed by requests for one approach and one paragraph. Coding agreement in five cases is not moral correctness or proof that generated reasons faithfully reveal internal decision processes. Full teacher data/coding are not available here.
findings.boundary: Evaluate factual premises, affected rights, alternatives and the connection between reasons and action. Ethical terminology, human modal agreement and fluent prose do not validate a conclusion or justify untested clinical/legal assumptions.

findings.definition: Context-sensitive judgment that integrates relevant knowledge, values and particular circumstances to decide what should be done.
findings.novelty_rationale: The study's contextual examples overlap the existing integrative judgment entry. Do not add its broad situational-ethics code as another synonym or assume it fully represents Fletcher's ethical theory.

evidence.quote: suggest broader rules to handle similar situations justly
proposing alternative ways to support the student

findings.evidence_scope: Examples combine student support with fairness and institutional constraints, including complementary recognition without grade inflation and a requested policy exception. These illustrate contextual reasoning, not a validated practical-wisdom measure or proven superiority over a rule-based alternative. The source's classifications can overlap.
findings.boundary: Flexibility is not automatically wisdom; an exception needs relevant grounds and fair treatment of comparable cases. Contextual reasoning, whim, favoritism and rationalization differ. Proposed school rules and exam eligibility are scenario premises, not independently checked legal facts.

findings.definition: Wording flips the answer; LLMs show this strongly, sometimes more than humans.
findings.novelty_rationale: Add an elicitation boundary to an existing concept rather than claiming a new prompt-induced bias without a controlled comparison.

evidence.quote: If you had to choose one approach
Would you choose deontological ethics here?

findings.evidence_scope: The supplied English summary contains leading alternatives and forced single-framework follow-ups. They are potential elicitation influences; there is no independent fresh-session, matched-wording or randomized prompt experiment. The original Turkish chat could not be read through the available share-page reader. This is not an additional direct framing-effect paper.
findings.boundary: Explaining a requested perspective or choosing among explicitly offered frameworks need not be sycophancy or a bias. Show a consequential, unsupported change under controlled semantically equivalent wording before attributing a framing effect.

source_corrections.issue: Regional counts do not match the stated sample total.
source_corrections.reliable_correction: The visibly printed values are Istanbul 58, Trabzon 19, Ankara 19, Yozgat 10, Erzurum 7 and Other 35, totaling 148, while the same legend and main methods say 141. If these are exclusive residence groups, the counts cannot all be correct. No corrected regional allocation can be recovered from the supplied article. Figure 2's school-type counts do total 141.

source_corrections.location: Table 2 and SUM explanation, PDF pages 9–10
source_corrections.issue: Some percentages exceed a single-response total while the methods explain only under-100 totals.
source_corrections.reliable_correction: Individual Needs/Collective Responsibility sums to 102.2% and Privacy/Professional Help to 101.4%. Missing or invalid answers alone cannot explain excess. Clarify multiple coding, denominators and valid counts; if codes are exclusive, the displayed values need correction. The displayed overall sum 798.5 differs from the footer's 797.87; unrounded outputs and coding counts are required before assigning a corrected total. Do not normalize away the ambiguity.

source_corrections.issue: AI 100% cells are attributed to using a single model.
source_corrections.reliable_correction: One model can produce different answers across runs and prompts. The cells describe the selected response/coding for each scenario, not 100% repeated agreement or deterministic model behavior. Report eight selected scenario responses and the absence of repeated-run frequency estimates.

source_corrections.location: Methods page 7 versus Appendix B pages 23–25
source_corrections.issue: Fresh-session and identical-condition language is not transparently reconciled with the summarized sequential conversation and additional model follow-ups.
source_corrections.reliable_correction: Document original prompt text, session boundaries, history, model snapshot/date and selection rules. Appendix B is explicitly an English summary, so it cannot alone reconstruct exact Turkish wording or definitively prove original session structure. A new account does not eliminate training bias or system-context influence. The linked original conversation was not readable in the available tool.

source_corrections.location: Results/discussion, teacher majority and significant differences
source_corrections.issue: Several modal codes below 50% are described as a majority, and qualitative differences as significant.
source_corrections.reliable_correction: Use plurality/modal category for 48.2%, 48.9%, 47.5%, 45.4% and 41.1%. Five-of-eight matching is descriptive category agreement, not an inferential significance test or ethical correctness. No reported aggregate result establishes the claimed effects of gender, experience or school level.

source_corrections.location: General AI/human mechanism claims, pages 1–4 and 18–20
source_corrections.issue: AI is broadly described as objective, consistent and outcome-oriented, while humans are portrayed as more empathic/contextual.
source_corrections.reliable_correction: The source also acknowledges training-data bias and presents AI context-sensitive reasons across several frameworks. Three selected responses are deontological, two virtue-ethical and one each social-justice, utilitarian and situational. No mechanism, empathy capacity, repeated consistency or superior pedagogical outcome is directly established by these examples. Retain the authors' critical-evaluation recommendation and avoid the universal dichotomy.

source_identity_checks.finding: The attached Reid/Petocz 2006 citation identifies University Lecturers’ Understanding of Sustainability, Higher Education 51:105–123, DOI 10.1007/s10734-004-6379-4. Its identity does not verify the nearby claim about contemporary AI big-data/predictive/process-automation capability. Recheck the full source and replace or supplement the attribution with a directly relevant source before relying on it.
source_identity_checks.scope: Bibliographic identity only; original full article unread. This is a relevance warning, not proof that every sentence is unrelated.

source_identity_checks.location: Ethical responsibility discussion page 3 and Malyshkin reference page 26
source_identity_checks.finding: Parallel Computing Technologies (2015), DOI 10.1007/978-3-319-21909-7, is an edited book/proceedings volume with Victor Malyshkin as editor. The paper supplies no supporting chapter/page for its nearby ethical-responsibility/regulation claim. Identify the actual supporting contribution rather than treating the volume's metadata as evidence.
source_identity_checks.scope: Book identity/editor only; no full book or chapter read and no assertion that the entire volume contains no ethics-related discussion.

methodological_limits: Snowball/purposive recruitment and teacher demographics do not establish a representative national comparison. The regional legend has an unresolved total mismatch.
One selected model, eight scenarios and follow-up elicitation do not yield model-level response probabilities, stable ethical dispositions or cross-model conclusions.
Ethical categories may overlap and self-named frameworks are not faithful process measures. Cooperative coding review is not independently quantified interrater reliability.
Qualitative modal agreement is not accuracy, moral legitimacy, causal evidence or a proof that disagreement is an AI error.
English summaries and a share URL do not reconstruct exact original prompts, translations, chat histories or output selection. The public share reader returned no conversation text.
The article supplies selected excerpts, not the complete teacher matrix or auditable codebook. Percentage denominators and multiple-code rules remain unclear.
Education training benefits, actual behavior, long-term learning, therapeutic outcomes and safeguarding/legal decisions are not tested. No real-world disclosure or medical recommendation is inferred.

cross_paper_learning.finding: Generated ethical reasons, scored scenario decisions, attention and durable norm internalization are different evidence levels. The present qualitative framework labels do not measure moral attentiveness or stable internalization.
A proposal that AI supports skill building is not a tested boost. This paper does not evaluate teacher learning after assistance removal or establish preserved independent competence.
Again separate hypothetical responses from actual behavior. Even plausible responsible counseling/transfer suggestions do not establish safe implementation or confirmed handover.

deferred.reason: The source defines it as contextual flexibility, overlapping existing practical wisdom. That summary does not establish the full Fletcher framework; avoid adding an oversimplified synonym.

A broad normative umbrella rather than one newly established psychological mechanism. Preserve rights/equality content in moral justification and specific reasoning entries instead of reproducing all five source coding buckets as nonoverlapping behaviors.
The model explains user-requested alternatives but retains its initial social-justice choice in the shown exchange. No independently established unwarranted agreement or controlled pressure effect.
The source discusses these values and capabilities, but selected textual reasons and category matches do not demonstrate felt empathy, eliminate bias or validate moral correctness.

limitations: Three additions are forms of ethical reasoning, not necessarily harmful behaviors. No automatic violation or harm edges are assigned.
No new yearly mention totals are measured, and no cited primary book or teacher study receives independent full-read credit from this review.
The ontology/catalogue is updated in place with stable IDs and existing categories on the draft research branch.
